tells.1: Templated Slack formatting: wave and clap emoji bookends, bolded label-colon bullets, and a stock 'Quick heads-up' opener with a 'Thanks, everyone! 🙌' close
tells.2: Uniformly polished, evenly parallel bullets with no personal voice. Reads like an AI-tidied version of the plain-prose versions
tells.3: Formulaic emoji-bookended bullet template plus the chirpy rhetorical close 'Got questions or feeling stuck?'
tells.6: Same templated emoji, bold and bullet scaffold as 3, plus a slightly garbled opener ('a quick heads-up about how we're handling repair tickets') that suggests a mechanical edit
tells.7: Mild: very even, symmetrical one-line paragraphs that feel lightly machine-smoothed, though there is no strong tell

reason: Version 4 reads like a competent person writing naturally, with a casual opener, plain paragraphs and a friendly 'we'll sort it out' close, and it states every date and action clearly. Version 5 is authentically human but clunky and formal, while 1, 3 and 6 carry the emoji-and-bold-bullet template typical of AI drafts.
